3. Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

3.1 Correlation Matrix

Before examining specific relationships, the full correlation matrix provides a holistic view of how key metrics relate:

Correlation Highlights: Discount percentage has a weak negative correlation with rating (r = -0.156) and a correlation of r = 0.011 with rating count. Actual price and discounted price are, as expected, very highly correlated. Discount percentage and actual price show a moderate positive relationship — more expensive items tend to have higher percentage discounts.

3.2 Discount vs. Customer Rating

Critical Insight: There is no meaningful positive relationship between discount depth and customer rating (r = -0.156). Deeper discounts do not translate into higher customer satisfaction. This challenges the common assumption that aggressive discounting improves perceived value.

3.3 Discount vs. Customer Engagement (Rating Count)

Engagement Finding: The correlation between discount percentage and rating count is r = 0.011. While there is a slight tendency for moderately discounted products to attract more reviews, the relationship is weak. Other factors (product type, brand, category demand) are likely stronger drivers of engagement.

4. Customer Engagement & Rating Distribution

4.1 Rating Distribution

Distribution Shape: Ratings are heavily left-skewed — the vast majority of products cluster between 4.0 and 4.5. The mean (4.10) and median (4.10) are close, confirming a consistently positive but slightly right-pulled distribution. Products below 3.5 are rare outliers.

4.2 Rating Count Distribution

Engagement Imbalance: The median rating count is just 5,179, but the mean is 18,307 — a massive gap indicating that a small number of products command the lion's share of customer engagement. The top 5% of products (by rating count) account for a disproportionate volume of all reviews.

Positive Dominance: 7,017 review titles (57.8%) contain positive sentiment keywords such as "good," "great," "excellent," and "value for money." Only 330 (2.7%) express negative sentiment.

5.2 Common Positive Themes

  • "Value for money" — the single most prevalent positive theme, appearing when products deliver at or above expectations for their price point.
  • "Good quality" — customers frequently highlight build quality and product durability.
  • "Fast charging" / "Works well" — functional performance is a key satisfier, especially in electronics and accessories.
  • "Easy to use" — usability and setup simplicity are notable positive differentiators.

5.3 Common Negative Themes

  • "Not working" / "Stopped working" — reliability and longevity are the top complaint drivers.
  • "Waste of money" — appears when products fail to meet the value expectation set by their price.
  • "Poor quality" — construction and material quality issues.
  • "Not as described" — expectation mismatch between product listing and actual product.

6. Strategic Recommendations

Each recommendation below is grounded in a specific data finding from this analysis.

1 Reallocate Discount Spend from Low-Impact to High-Engagement Segments
The weak negative correlation (r = -0.156) between discount depth and rating proves that deeper discounts do not improve customer satisfaction. Instead of broad-based discounting, concentrate promotional budgets on price segments where discounts show the strongest engagement lift — specifically the ₹500–₹2,000 mid-range where moderate discounts (20–40%) already show favorable rating and review volume outcomes.
Supporting data: Discount-to-rating correlation r = -0.156; mid-range products average 4.09 rating with 46.0% average discount.
2 Investigate and Address Quality Issues in Car&Motorbike
Car&Motorbike has the lowest category rating at 3.80, below the catalog average of 4.10. Conduct a deep-dive into product-level reviews within this category to identify recurring defects or expectation mismatches. Consider delisting or replacing consistently underperforming SKUs to protect catalog quality scores.
Supporting data: Car&Motorbike avg rating = 3.80 vs. catalog avg = 4.10 (-0.30 delta). Product count: 1.
3 Double Down on OfficeProducts — the Proven Satisfaction Leader
OfficeProducts leads with a 4.31 average rating across 31 products. Expand assortment in this category and use its high satisfaction as a competitive differentiator in marketing. Products here demonstrate that customers reward quality over discount depth.
Supporting data: OfficeProducts avg rating = 4.31, avg discount = 12.4%, 31 products.
4 Reduce the Long Tail of Low-Engagement Products
With a median rating count of only 5,179 against a mean of 18,307, a substantial portion of the catalog receives near-zero customer engagement. Audit products with fewer than 50 ratings and ratings below 3.8 — these represent dead weight in the catalog. Consider consolidating overlapping SKUs and redirecting visibility toward proven winners.
Supporting data: Median rating count = 5,179; mean = 18,307. 40 products have fewer than 50 ratings.
5 Improve Product Listing Accuracy to Reduce "Not as Described" Complaints
Sentiment analysis reveals "not as described" as a recurring negative theme. This is a fixable problem: enhance product descriptions, add more representative images, and implement A/B testing on listing content for products with high return rates or low ratings. Accurate listings reduce negative reviews and build long-term trust, which — per the data — drives engagement more effectively than discounting.
Supporting data: Negative sentiment reviews comprise 2.7% of all review titles; "not as described" is a top negative theme.
